piece_type: DTC TV ad and DTC desktop display banner

cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: “When added to an antidepressant, REXULTI was proven to reduce depression symptoms 62% more than the antidepressant alone.” (Voiceover, frames 8-9) | “When added to an antidepressant, Rexulti was proven to provide a 62% greater reduction in depression symptoms” (Frame 3) | “When added to an antidepressant, Rexulti was proven to provide a 62% greater reduction in depression symptoms vs. the antidepressant alone.” (Frame 4)
cases.context: Placebo-subtracted MADRS difference -3.2 from baseline 27 = 11.9% (Study 1); 4.8%/7.4% in Study 2; 'Individual results may vary' does not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Relative difference of change scores presented as a 62% symptom reduction greatly overstates benefit.
cases.check: Rule: flag '% more/greater reduction' claims derived from ratios of change scores; recompute as placebo-subtracted difference relative to baseline.
